questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Are approaching a railroad crossing and should prepare to stop.

Should stop and wait for a signal before crossing the railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are approaching a railroad crossing and should prepare to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A round sign means a railroad crossing is ahead. This sign is posted a few hundred feet before the tracks. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

options.text: Drivers must bear either right or left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You should stop for other traffic.

Traffic is entering from another road and you should keep right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is entering from another road and you should allow additional space for drivers to merge safely into the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign alerts you that traffic will merge into your lane ahead. Check your mirrors and side, then move to another lane if possible to give merging drivers space.

options.text: There is a 35 mph speed zone after the curve ahead.

Approach the upcoming curve at a speed of 35 mph or slower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the upcoming curve at a speed of 35 mph or slower.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert you to immediate conditions. Speed advisory plaques accompany these signs to show the safe speed for the upcoming curve.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangular signs mean yield. Slow down when you see a yield sign and stop if needed. If you stop, do so at the marked line.
